references.text: The fulfillment of Moses' promise to spread out his hands to the Lord so that the thunder and hail would cease.
Solomon spreads out his hands toward heaven in prayer to the Lord, the same gesture of prayer used by Moses.
Description of spreading out one's hands in prayer to God.
Declaration that the earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord, the same theological point Moses conveys to Pharaoh.
God declares that the world and everything in it is His.
Similar purpose: 'so that you may know' that the Lord is God.
The Lord declares that the whole earth belongs to Him.
The heavens and the earth belong to the Lord your God.
Reference to spreading out one's hands in prayer to God.
Paul quotes that the earth and everything in it belongs to the Lord.
Both verses illustrate Moses' strategic withdrawal to pray for the plagues to cease, showing the role of prayer in God's judgment.
Both verses highlight Moses as an intercessor who goes to the Lord to intervene and change the situation for others.
Both verses show Moses using a hand gesture to trigger God's judgment over His enemies (the sea/hail).
Direct narrative connection where 9:23 describes the start of the hail plague and 9:29 describes how it ceases through prayer.
